Um, I'm current, um, I, well, in my, in my teacher's classroom, the, um, one of her, um, I guess the teacher's assistant referred me, and she said that she also started here, and this is what helped her get into it.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
Well, I used to work as a behavior technique. So I, my consumer, he was five years, five years old, and he didn't want to do the work that he had to do. He would get mad and start throwing stuff. So I try to help him relax. And I first did what he wanted to do. And we came to a conclusion that we would do 10 minutes, what he wanted to do, and then 10 minutes back to work. And that helped him balance everything out. And it helped him get used to doing the work as well.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
A time that I was stressed out is when I couldn't get the client to come and sit down and they were just running around or trying to hit like the teachers. So what I would do, I would take him outside and I would just like talk to him and calm him down and then go back inside and we would try it again in the corner, like just us two.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or saying no. Walk me through exactly what you would do, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
I would first try to calm them down and explain to them what I'm going to do or what's going to happen and just let them relax and then I will try to like put on their diaper and talk to them through it or try like to make them laugh through it so that they don't be too overwhelmed.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something didn’t go as planned at work and your role in it. How did you handle the responsibility piece?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q7 Attempt 1]
something that didn't go as planned during work something that didn't go as planned is probably putting two siblings together and working with them together that became kind of overwhelmed and for the parents or for the consumer too my role was to get the two since the siblings were not really close to each other and couldn't be in the same room together my my i had to get them used to them being in the same room and relaxing them so what i would do is i would um do like an arts craft where the both of them would take turns in it and that's how they got used to working together or we would also do games where it would be like them too against me in a way or with mom as well

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you had to work closely with another adult in a challenging situation. How did you navigate it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:

So me and the other teacher, we would go in and try to relax them and trying to let them know that that's not okay and then trying to redirect them.
